site.title: Yanagi Hygiene
site.tagline: Commercial pest management from Collingwood, Melbourne, since 2011.

pages.title: Home
About Us
pages.content:
Yanagi Hygiene was founded in 2011 by Hana Yanagi, a former hospital infection-control officer who thought commercial pest control relied too much on spraying and too little on looking. She opened a small depot at 41 Wellington Street, Collingwood, and built the firm around one hour of careful inspection and a short, honest plan.

Today fourteen people work from the depot: field technicians for kitchens, hotels, warehouses and docks, a records and reports lead who writes every findings sheet template, an entomologist who reviews identification, and a client desk that books the hour and the year. We serve sites within 60 km of Collingwood.

Why one hour first

A plan written before anyone has looked is a guess. The inspection hour gives you a signed findings sheet on the day, and the hour is credited to your first year if a plan starts within 30 days.

Why records

Every visit leaves a signed sheet on site and a full report by email within two working days. We keep records for the life of your plan plus three years, so an auditor can see what we saw and when.

pages.title: Season List
pages.content:
Four emails a year, one before each visit season, with early inspection-hour slots for new sites. No newsletters in between, and no sharing of your address.

To join, write to desk@yanagihygiene.example with the words “season list” and the suburb of your site. Grace at the client desk will confirm within one working day.

pages.title: Request an Inspection Hour
pages.content:
Tell us the site type, the floor area, the suburb and a time window that suits your trading hours. We reply within 1 working day and hold the inspection hour within 5 working days. Findings are left on site at the end of the hour, and the full report is emailed within 2 working days.

Desk and visits

Desk Mon–Fri 07:00–18:00, Sat 08:00–12:00 (Melbourne time), closed Sundays and public holidays. Inspections and visits are booked 05:30–23:00, any day, around your trading hours.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
Plans run 12 months and either side can end them with 30 days’ notice. All prices are in AUD and include GST.

Inspection hour AUD 180 (credited to the first year if a plan starts within 30 days). Café and small kitchen AUD 1,480 a year, restaurant and food production AUD 2,640 a year, office building AUD 1,960 a year, warehouse and dock AUD 3,420 a year, hotel and mixed-use from AUD 6,900 a year. Call-out between visits AUD 220 per visit, included on 12-visit plans.

We promise visits, looking, records and a plan. We do not promise a pest-free building.

posts.title: Why the first hour starts at the loading dock
posts.excerpt: Most of what enters a building arrives through one door, so that is where we look first.
posts.content:
Every building has one door where the outside comes in, and for most of our sites it is the loading dock. Pallets arrive, wrap and cardboard collect in a corner, and a rubber seal that has worn by a few millimetres lets in more than the weather.

In the first ten minutes of an inspection hour we ask where deliveries arrive. Then we go there with a torch and a slim gap gauge and we measure. A seal gap of nine millimetres goes on the findings sheet with a number and a place on your floor plan. It is dull work, and it is the work that decides the plan.

posts.title: What we teach new technicians in their first week
posts.excerpt: Looking, writing it down and reading a floor plan come before any product.
posts.content:
New technicians spend their first week with a floor plan and a torch, not a canister. Jonas Weber, our entomologist, teaches identification from photographs and from the monitors that come back from the field.

Priya Nair then shows them the findings sheet. If a point is not on the sheet with a number, it did not happen. By Friday every new colleague has walked a site with Hana Yanagi and written one sheet that Priya has read line by line.

posts.title: Bin stores after a long weekend
posts.excerpt: Lids, drains and washdown points tell you most of what you need to know.
posts.content:
A shared bin store is where an office plan is often decided. After a long weekend, lids are left up, drains hold water and bags sit a day longer than planned.

We check the lid seals, lift the drain cover and look at the washdown point. We note what we found, and what your team can change, on a single page before we leave.

posts.title: Rooftop plant rooms in late spring
posts.excerpt: Netting, duct penetrations and roof access are checked every season.
posts.content:
Late spring is when birds look for sheltered ledges, and a plant room has plenty. Our May and August visits include the netting edge, the duct penetrations and the roof hatch.

We photograph nothing that is not on the plan, and we write down what we see rather than what we expect. The next visit date goes on the sheet before we leave.
